entries.subject: DAMIT 441: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-441.txt. Model 441, version 2011-10-27, pole (258°, -42°), period 10.40828 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: R. D. Stephens (2012), A shape model of the main-belt asteroid 27 Euterpe
entries.finding: [R. D. Stephens (2012), A shape model of the main-belt asteroid 27 Euterpe](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012MPBu...39....2S) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — included as an explicitly approximate thermal size transfer. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 109.79 ± 1.54 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 27 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.

entries.subject: Resolved-model surveys: body-specific candidate not established
entries.finding: The imported survey cites Hanuš 2017, Viikinkoski 2017 and Vernazza 2021 without identifying a selected product for this body. The current DAMIT reference join does not bind selected model 441 to those surveys. This does not prove that no resolved model exists elsewhere; a body-specific candidate and its release must be identified before the entry can count as included.
entries.revisitWhen: A target row, supplementary model or release URL from one of these surveys establishes a concrete candidate and permits comparison with the selected shape.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: The display scale "54.895 km (approximate thermal scale)" (akari-acua-v1) implies a diameter of 109.79 km, outside the added Small Bodies Occultations V4.0 record 24, DAMIT model 441 diameter 107 ± 1 km (volume-equivalent; DAMIT model 441 fitted to 2 occultations). Both are shown; the display scale is not changed.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.
